TADA_AutoClean powerful function performs variety tasks including: (1) creating new “TADA” prefixed columns capitalizing contents reduce case sensitivity issues, (2) converts special characters value columns, (3) converts latitude longitude values numeric, (4) replaces “meters” “m”, (5) replaces deprecated characteristic names current WQX names, (6) harmonizes result detection limit units WQX, TADA user supplied target units, (7) converts depths meters, (8) creates column TADA.ComparableDataIdentifier concatenating characteristic name, result sample fraction, method speciation, result measure unit. TADA TADA_FlagCoordinates function identifies flags potentially invalid coordinate data. functionality showcased , always important review invalid outputs cleaning reduce risk leaving usable data/sites. Allowable values clean_outsideUSA “”, “remove”, “change sign”. default “” flags latitude longitude coordinates outside USA. Assigning clean_ousideUSA = “remove” remove rows data coordinates outside USA. assigning clean_outsideUSA = “change sign” flip sign latitude longitude coordinates flagged outside USA. “change sign” option used known coordinates entered wrong sign WQX; additionally, data owner fix incorrect coordinates raw data WQX - assistance email WQX help desk: WQX@epa.gov Allowable values clean_imprecise TRUE FALSE. default FALSE flags rows data invalid imprecise coordinates without removing . Assigning clean_imprecise = TRUE remove rows data invalid imprecise coordinates. Allowable values flaggedonly TRUE FALSE. default FALSE keeps rows data regardless flag status. Assigning flaggedonly = TRUE filters dataframe show rows data flagged. clean_outsideUSA = “” /clean_imprecise = FALSE, column appended titled “TADA.InvalidCoordinates.Flag” following flags (relevant dataframe): latitude less zero, row flagged “LAT_OutsideUSA”. (Exception American Samoa) longitude greater zero less 145, row flagged “LONG_OutsideUSA”. (Exceptions Guam Northern Mariana Islands) latitude longitude contains string, “999”, row flagged invalid. Finally, precision can measured number decimal places latitude longitude provided. either numbers right decimal point, row flagged “Imprecise”.

TADA_IDCensoredData - categorizes detection limit data identifies mismatches result detection condition result detection limit type. function runs within TADA_SimpleCensoredMethods function. words, detection limit information copied pasted result value column original value NA detection limit information available. two columns TADA focuses define flag censored data ResultDetectionConditionText DetectionQuantitationLimitTypeName. TADA package currently functions summarize censored data incidence dataset perform simple substitutions censored data values, including x times detection limit random selection value 0 detection limit. user may specify methods used non-detects -detects separately input TADA_SimpleCensoredMethods function. censored data functions depend first TADA_IDCensoredData utility function, assigns TADA.CensoredData.Flag data records identifies -detects non-detects using ResultDetectionConditionText DetectionQuantitationLimitTypeName. utility function automatically run within TADA_DataRetrieval function produces TADA.CensoredData.Flag column. records receive one following classifications: - Uncensored - filled detection limit value; detection. - Non-Detect - Left-censored - -Detect - Right-censored - Condition/Limit Populated - detection condition limit type ambiguous associated lower/upper detection limit. - Conflict Condition Limit - detection condition limit type single record agree, e.g. one suggests -detect suggests non-detect. - Detection condition detection limit documented TADA reference tables. - detection condition limit type characterized TADA reference tables, based WQX domain tables. - Detection condition missing required censored data ID. - Result needs information categorized. text: TADA_GetSynonymRef function generates synonym reference table specific input dataframe. Users can review input data relates standard TADA values following elements: TADA.CharacteristicName TADA.ResultSampleFractionText TADA.MethodSpeciationName TADA.ResultMeasure.MeasureUnitCode Users can also edit reference file meet needs desired. download argument can used save harmonization file current working directory download = TRUE, default download = FALSE. TADA_HarmonizeSynonyms function compares input dataframe TADA Synonym Reference Table makes conversions target characteristics/fractions/speciations/units provided. function also appends column called TADA.Harmonized.Flag, indicating results metadata changed/converted function. purpose function make similar data consistent therefore easier compare analyze. examples TADA_HarmonizeSynonyms function can used: TADA.ResultSampleFractionText specifies forms constituents. cases, single TADA.CharacteristicName “Total” “Dissolved” forms specified, combined. cases, TADA.CharacteristicName TADA.ResultSampleFractionText combination given different identifier. identifier can used later identify comparable data groups calculating statistics creating figures combination. variables different names represent constituent (e.g., “Total Kjeldahl nitrogen (Organic N & NH3)” “Kjeldahl nitrogen”). TADA_HarmonizeSynonyms function gives consistent name (identifier) synonyms.

text: section covers summing nutrient subspecies estimate total nitrogen phosphorus. can challenging endeavor subspecies/compounds overlap total nutrient calculations. TADA adds one equation mix: total particulate nitrogen + total dissolved nitrogen. function uses many subspecies possible calculate total given site, date, depth group, estimate total nitrogen whatever subspecies present. function creates NEW total nutrient measurements (total nitrogen unfiltered N total phosphorus unfiltered P) adds dataframe. code: The TADA R Shiny application can be run [on the web](https://rconnect-public.epa.gov/TADAShiny/) (R and R Studio install not required), or within R Studio. We recommend running it within R Studio if possible to avoid time out issues (especially when working with large datasets) and to make sure you are using the most up to date version. The web version of the application is on a slightly lagged update schedule. Run the following code within R Studio to install or update and run the most recent version of the [TADA R Shiny](https://github.com/USEPA/TADAShiny) application:  ```{r} if(!"remotes"%in%installed.packages()){ install.packages("remotes") }  library(remotes)  remotes::install_github("USEPA/TADAShiny", ref = "develop", dependencies = TRUE, force = TRUE)  library(TADAShiny)  run_app()

title: TADA_AutoClean — TADA_AutoClean
text: function performs following tasks: Creates new columns TADA prefix "TADA." capitalizes letters within interoperable WQX validation reference tables reduce issues case-sensitivity joining data: CharacteristicName, ResultSampleFractionText, MethodSpeciationName, ResultMeasure.MeasureUnitCode, ActivityMediaName, DetectionQuantitationLimitMeasure.MeasureUnitCode. function runs "TADA_ConvertSpecialChars" columns: ResultMeasureValue DetectionQuantitationLimitMeasure.MeasureValue. Replace meters" “m” following columns: TADA.ResultMeasure.MeasureUnitCode, ActivityDepthHeightMeasure.MeasureUnitCode, ActivityTopDepthHeightMeasure.MeasureUnitCode, ActivityBottomDepthHeightMeasure.MeasureUnitCode, ResultDepthHeightMeasure.MeasureUnitCode. Runs TADA_SubstituteDeprecatedChars replace deprecated characteristic names based Water Quality Exchange (WQX) Characteristic domain table. Runs TADA_ConvertResultUnits harmonize result detection limit units WQX TADA user supplied target units. Enter ?TADA_ConvertResultUnits ?TADA_CreateUnitRef() console details. Runs TADA_ConvertDepthUnits convert depth units meters following columns: ResultDepthHeightMeasure.MeasureValue, ActivityDepthHeightMeasure.MeasureValue, ActivityTopDepthHeightMeasure.MeasureValue, ActivityBottomDepthHeightMeasure.MeasureValue, add new columns “TADA” prefix. Runs TADA_CreateComparableID create comparable data group concatenating TADA.CharacteristicName, TADA.ResultSampleFractionText, TADA.MethodSpeciationName, TADA.ResultMeasure.MeasureUnitCode.

UseParamRef_UT2 <- TADA_CreateUseParamRef(   Data_Nutrients_UT,   paramRef = paramRef_UT4, org_id = c("UTAHDWQ"), excel = FALSE )  # Let's test the "auto_assign" input UseParamRef_UT3 <- TADA_CreateUseParamRef(   Data_Nutrients_UT,   paramRef = paramRef_UT4, auto_assign = TRUE, org_id = c("UTAHDWQ"), excel = FALSE ) #> [1] "auto_assign == TRUE was selected, assigning all unique ATTAINS.UseName, by ATTAINS.OrganizationIdentifier, to any ATTAINS.ParameterName that an organization have not done assessments for in prior ATTAINS cycle. text: Function generates synonym reference table containing unique combinations TADA.CharacteristicName, TADA.ResultSampleFractionText, TADA.MethodSpeciationName. function also joins TADA-specific suggested synonyms nutrients priority parameters. target synonyms (denoted reference table prefix "Target.") intended help user aggregate synonymous data may uploaded slightly different metadata conventions prepare nutrient data total N P summations. Users can review input data relates target synonyms TADA.CharacteristicName, TADA.ResultSampleFractionText, TADA.MethodSpeciationName. synonym table created, users may optionally edit target columns reference table meet needs. Additionally, function assumes user already removed data containing suspect characteristic-unit-fraction-speciation combinations (.e. user already run TADA_FlagFraction, TADA_FlagSpeciation, TADA_FlagResultUnit, etc.).

text: function uses WQX Characteristic domain table substitute deprecated (.e. retired /suspect) Characteristic Names new name TADA.CharacteristicName column. TADA_SubstituteDeprecatedChars run within TADA_AutoClean, runs within TADA_DataRetrieval (autoclean = TRUE) TADA_BigDataRetrieval. Therefore, deprecated characteristic names harmonized new name automatically upon data retrieval. TADA_SubstituteDeprecatedChars can also used user supplied dataset WQX/WQP format, desired. solution works EPA WQX USGS NWIS provided data.

title: Substitute Preferred Characteristic Name for Deprecated Names — TADA_SubstituteDeprecatedChars
code: TADA_SubstituteDeprecatedChars(.data)

title: Substitute Preferred Characteristic Name for Deprecated Names — TADA_SubstituteDeprecatedChars
text: .data TADA dataframe

title: Substitute Preferred Characteristic Name for Deprecated Names — TADA_SubstituteDeprecatedChars
text: Input TADA dataframe substituted characteristic names TADA.CharacteristicName column. Original columns unchanged.

title: Substitute Preferred Characteristic Name for Deprecated Names — TADA_SubstituteDeprecatedChars
text: Enter ?TADA_GetCharacteristicRef() review list WQX characteristics, including deprecated names (Char_Flag). can used crosswalk deprecated names (CharacteristicName) new names (Comparable.Name).

title: Substitute Preferred Characteristic Name for Deprecated Names — TADA_SubstituteDeprecatedChars
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ # download nutrient data in MT from 2022 and set autoclean = FALSE df <- TADA_DataRetrieval(   startDate = "2022-01-01",   endDate = "2022-12-31",   characteristicType = "Nutrient",   statecode = "MT",   applyautoclean = FALSE, ask = FALSE ) df2 <- TADA_SubstituteDeprecatedChars(df) # in this example, "Inorganic nitrogen (nitrate and nitrite)" is a USGS NWIS # characteristic that is deprecated and # "Phosphate-phosphorus***retired***use Total Phosphorus, mixed forms" # is a deprecated WQX name. Both are are transformed to their new names. # review characteristic names before and after transformation unique(df2$CharacteristicName) unique(df2$TADA.CharacteristicName)  df3 <- TADA_DataRetrieval(   startDate = "2022-01-01", endDate = "2022-12-31",   characteristicType = "Nutrient", statecode = "WY", applyautoclean = FALSE,   ask = FALSE ) df4 <- TADA_SubstituteDeprecatedChars(df3) unique(df4$CharacteristicName) unique(df4$TADA.CharacteristicName) } # }

title: Create or Update Monitoring Location Identifier and Assessment Unit Identifier Crosswalk in ATTAINS — TADA_UpdateMonitoringLocationsInATTAINS
text: org_id Character argument. ATTAINS organization identifier must supplied user. list organization identifiers can found downloading ATTAINS Domains Excel file: https://www.epa.gov/system/files/-files/2025-02/domains_2025-02-25.xlsx. Organization identifiers listed "OrgName" tab. "code" column contains organization identifiers used param. crosswalk user-supplied dataframe columns ASSESSMENT_UNIT_ID, MS_LOCATION_ID, MS_ORG_ID, MONITORING_DATA_LINK_TEXT required. ASSESSMENT_UNIT_ID MS_LOCATION_ID must filled order use function. additional columns, MONITORING_DATA_LINK_TEXT, containing single URL "; " separated URLs linking information monitoring location, MS_ORG_ID, containing WQP organization identifier monitoring location can left blank function still run. Data link URLS WQP site pages automatically generated function unless MS_ORG_ID column populated WQP OrganizationIdentifier. crosswalk = NULL, crosswalk downloaded ATTAINS. allows users add URLs Water Quality Portal data site pages ATTAINS assessment unit profile possible without updating information ATTAINS. attains_replace Character argument. attains_replace = FALSE, Monitoring Location Identifiers user supplied crosswalk appended existing ATTAINS crosswalk. attains_replace = TRUE, Monitoring Location Identifiers retained user supplied crosswalk. Default equals FALSE. wqp_data_links Character argument. wqp_data_links equal "add" "replace", function build URL Water Quality Portal Data Site page Monitoring Location Identifier data frame. examine response code URL retain 200 response, indicates URL valid. wqp_data_links = "add", URL added existing text MS_DATA_LINK_TEXT column. wqp_data_links = "replace", URL replace existing text MS_DATA_LINK_TEXT column. wqp_data_links = "none", URLs created added returned data frame. Default wqp_data_links = "add".

code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ # Alaska example to updated data links with no user supplied crosswalk AK_adddatalinks <- TADA_UpdateMonitoringLocationsInATTAINS(   org_id = "AKDECWQ",   crosswalk = NULL,   attains_replace = FALSE,   wqp_data_links = "replace" )  # Alaska example using a user supplied crosswalk to update entries in # ATTAINS by appending user supplied information to ATTAINS crosswalk  # example monitoring location identifiers ASSESSMENT_UNIT_ID <- c(   "AK_M_1021211_000", "AK_M_1021008_000",   "AK_M_1021109_013", "AK_M_1021109_013",   "AK_M_1021109_013" )  # example organization identifiers MS_ORG_ID <- c("AKDECWQ", "AKDECWQ", "AKDECWQ", "AKDECWQ", "AKDECWQ")  # example assessment units MS_LOCATION_ID <- c(   "ExampleSite1", "ExampleSite2", "ExampleSite3",   "ExampleSite4", "ExampleSite5" ) # example urls MONITORING_DATA_LINK_TEXT <- c(   "https://www.waterqualitydata.us/provider/STORET/AKDECWQ/",   "https://www.waterqualitydata.us/provider/STORET/AKDECWQ/",   "https://www.waterqualitydata.us/provider/STORET/AKDECWQ/",   "https://www.waterqualitydata.us/provider/STORET/AKDECWQ/",   "https://www.waterqualitydata.us/provider/STORET/AKDECWQ/" )  # create example crosswalk data frame ex.user.cw <- data.frame(   MS_LOCATION_ID, MS_ORG_ID, ASSESSMENT_UNIT_ID,   MONITORING_DATA_LINK_TEXT )  AK_appenduserdata <- TADA_UpdateMonitoringLocationsInATTAINS(   org_id = "AKDECWQ",   crosswalk = ex.user.cw,   attains_replace = FALSE,   wqp_data_links = "none" ) } # }
